text:
Evidence supports testing objectives before changing representations. [gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses partly to overconfidence from sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) identifies informative negative gradients and top-K ranking benefits. [Correcting LogQ (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampling correction: the designated positive is always included, unlike sampled negatives; treating both identically introduces bias. Correction must match the actual sampling construction, particularly with popularity-distributed in-batch negatives.

Hardness requires control. [Enhanced BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) explicitly addresses false negatives that mislead hard-negative training; [adaptive hardness sampling (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) investigates adapting difficulty rather than always choosing the hardest item. These findings motivate—not establish—a uniform-plus-moderately-hard mixture, warm-up, and masking known training positives. Unknown future preferences remain unobservable; high model scores alone cannot establish whether an item is a true negative.

For this benchmark, a useful controlled ablation is unchanged SASRec with multi-negative sampled softmax, generalized BCE, then a controlled hard-negative mixture, comparing all four categories under matched GPU budgets and fixed macro validation HR@10. Electronics’ weaker margins do not identify the cause. Keep the host’s 99-negative evaluator unchanged: [sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation. Therefore, validation gains support this candidate protocol, not automatically better full-catalog recommendations.
